subject: zoom in on a spectro plot in both time and amplitude?

messages.author: bc60ed1bc4b67b7d
messages.subject: zoom in on a spectro plot in both time and amplitude?
parts:
I'm a total novice on seewave - tried to solve this on my own for a couple of days.

I am displaying a wave file in a plot, I want to "zoom in" on the plot to display the part of interest (in this case, a bird call).  I've learned how to read in part of the wave file by a range of time, effectively zooming in on the time axis.  How can I zoom in on the aplitude axis, such that I display only from, say 0 to 3 kHz in this example?  what if I only wanted to display something in the middle (e.g., in this example, 3-4 kHz)?

# ----------------
# grabbing file off of online repository:
url <- "http://www.xeno-canto.org/13605/download"
file <- "113605.mp3"
download.file(url, destfile=file, quiet=TRUE)
flammulated_owl <- readMP3(file)

# convert to wave file
savewav(flammulated_owl, f=44100, filename = "flammulated_owl_conv.wav", rescale=c(-1500,1500)) #convert the mp3 to wav

#read in the .wav file created from .mp3
flamowl <- readWave("flammulated_owl_conv.wav")
# crop time to the first 1 second, to zoom in on call
flamowl_crop <- readWave("flammulated_owl_conv.wav", from=0, to=1, units="seconds")

spectro(flamowl, osc=TRUE) # original file
spectro(flamowl_crop, osc=TRUE) # cropped in time to 0-1 second
#------------

messages.author: 1f04514119422e67
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] zoom in on a spectro plot in both time and amplitude?
parts:
You can use the parameter flim to determine which part of the spectrogram will be plotted on the frequency axis (in kHz), and tlim will do the same for the time axis (in seconds). Both parameters take a two element vector as in c(start, finish)

spectro(flamowl, osc=TRUE, flim = c(0,3))

Cheers,
Vitor
